summary: The Department of Foreign Affairs says nationals of the countries it lists under Executive Order No. 408 may enter the Philippines without a visa for an initial stay of 30 days, with a passport valid at least six months beyond the stay and a return or onward ticket; the Bureau of Immigration handles extensions at its offices. Arriving passengers, except foreign diplomats and dignitaries, 9(e) visa holders and holders of diplomatic or official passports, must register on the free eTravel platform, which allows registration within 72 hours before arrival.

CN.notes: The Philippine visa policy says Chinese nationals may enter without a visa for a non-extendible and non-convertible period of 14 days for tourism and business, on presenting a passport valid at least six months beyond the intended stay, a confirmed hotel booking and a return or onward ticket, and only through Ninoy Aquino International Airport (Metro Manila) or Mactan-Cebu International Airport (Cebu).

quote.text: Chinese nationals may enter the Philippines without a visa for a non-extendible and non-convertible period of 14 days for tourism and business purposes, subject to the following conditions: Presentation of a passport valid for at least six (6) months beyond the intended stay; Confirmed hotel accommodation or booking; and A return or onward ticket to the next country of destination. Entry under this visa-free privilege shall be allowed only through the following designated ports of entry: Ninoy Aquino International Airport, Metro Manila Mactan-Cebu International Airport, Cebu

IN.notes: The Philippine visa policy says Indian nationals may enter without a visa for a non-extendible and non-convertible period of 14 days for tourism and business, with a passport valid at least six months beyond the stay, a confirmed hotel booking, proof of financial capacity and a return or onward ticket. Indian nationals holding a valid American, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore or UK visa or residence permit may enter without a visa for a non-extendible period of 30 days for tourism, with a passport valid at least six months beyond the stay and a return or onward ticket.

quote.text: Indian nationals may enter the Philippines without a visa for a non-extendible and non-convertible period of 14 days for tourism and business purposes, upon presenting a passport valid for at least six (6) months beyond the contemplated stay, confirmed hotel accommodation / booking, proof of financial capacity, and return or onward ticket to the next country of destination. Indian nationals holding valid and current American, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore or United Kingdom (AJACSSUK) visas or residence permits may enter the Philippines without a visa for a non-extendible period of 30 days for tourism, upon presenting a passport valid for at least six (6) months beyond the contemplated stay, and return or onward ticket to the next country of destination.

tips.text: The Department of Foreign Affairs says visa-free nationals must possess return tickets to their country of origin or outward-bound tickets to their next country of destination, and the UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for proof of return or onward travel.
The eTravel FAQ says etravel.gov.ph is the only official eTravel website, that registration is free of charge, and to beware of fake or scam websites that require payment.

After the initial 30 days, the Bureau of Immigration lists an initial 29-day extension (the visa waiver), then extensions beyond 59 days by 1 or 2 months, or a Long-Stay Visitor Extension of not more than six months; it refers to a maximum allowable stay of 36 months for visa-non-required nationals.

The UK government says around 20 typhoons hit the Philippines each year, mostly between June and November, and Canada says local authorities may suspend ferry services on short notice when a storm signal is raised, that you could get stranded at ports for several days, and to plan for extra time, especially during the rainy season.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: No. The United States is on the Department of Foreign Affairs' list of countries whose nationals may enter without a visa for an initial stay of 30 days, with a passport valid at least six months beyond the stay and a return or onward ticket. The Bureau of Immigration handles extensions of stay. Arriving passengers must also register on eTravel, which allows registration within 72 hours before arrival.

faq.question: What is eTravel and who needs it?
faq.answer: eTravel (etravel.gov.ph, its only official website) is a free digital data collection platform for passengers arriving in and departing from the Philippines. Arriving passengers, foreign or Filipino, must register, except foreign diplomats and their dependants, foreign dignitaries, 9(e) visa holders and holders of diplomatic and official or service passports. Registration is possible within 72 hours before arrival; the QR code is shown to the airline before boarding and to customs on arrival.

faq.question: Is an onward ticket really required for the Philippines?
faq.answer: Yes, for visa-free visitors. The Department of Foreign Affairs' visa policy says visa-free nationals must possess return tickets to their country of origin or outward-bound tickets to their next country of destination. The UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for proof of return or onward travel, and Canada says customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket.

faq.question: How do I extend my stay in the Philippines?
faq.answer: The Bureau of Immigration says visa-free tourists admitted for 30 days apply for an initial extension of 29 days (the visa waiver, PHP 3,030) at its main office or other authorised immigration offices. It lists further extensions of authorized stay beyond 59 days by 1 or 2 months, and a Long-Stay Visitor Extension of not more than six months, and refers to a maximum allowable stay of 36 months for visa-non-required nationals.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: Not for short visits. The Department of Foreign Affairs says Indian nationals may enter visa-free for a non-extendible and non-convertible period of 14 days for tourism and business, with a passport valid at least six months beyond the stay, confirmed hotel accommodation, proof of financial capacity and a return or onward ticket. Those holding valid US, Japanese, Australian, Canadian, Schengen, Singapore or UK visas or residence permits may enter visa-free for a non-extendible period of 30 days for tourism.
